description: We are 3rd year Computer Science students from Silesian University of Technology.
summary: Health Monitor is an app that allows astronauts to track their own health. It consists of: colour-coded vital signs, a body profile showing what's working well, graphs covering the entire mission, fitness test and ECG results, a well-being questionnaire, cognitive tests, daily tasks with points and badges, and simple explanations of each measurement. It also features a visualisation of satellites on a world map showing their current position.
details: Health Monitor helps astronauts on long missions spot health problems early. It shows vital signs in green, amber or red on a body map, alongside fitness and ECG results, a mood questionnaire, cognitive tests, and daily health tasks with points. It also tracks the ISS live. How: A physiological model generates realistic data with injected problems, like fever or low oxygen, and logs each one so we can check that alerts catch it. Thresholds come from NASA and clinical norms. Impact: More independent astronauts, and possible use at polar stations or for health monitoring at home. Tools: JavaScript (React, Node.js), SQLite, Python, and CelesTrak satellite data. It runs in a browser. We considered: privacy (all data is synthetic), false alarms, accessibility and simplicity.
